standard_prerequisites.use: The numeral for m applies its argument D exactly m times, so H at numerals n and m reduces to the second projection of the m-fold iterate of D at the initial pair.

core_obligations: Set up the encoding (proof lines 1163-1177): with h defined from f and g by primitive recursion, define H = lambda x y. Snd (y D (0, F x)) with D = lambda p. pair of (Succ (Fst p)) and (G x (Fst p) (Snd p)); the state pair carries the current y and the current h-value; the author gives the construction for a single additional argument x as a declared simplification.
Prove the induction base (proof lines 1184-1189): the zero-fold iterate of D at the initial pair (0, F n) is that pair, and since F lambda-defines f and f(n) = h(n,0) it reduces to (0, h(n,0)).

Prove the induction step and conclude (proof lines 1191-1224): assuming the m-fold iterate reduces to (m, h(n,m)), one more application of D reduces it to (m+1, g(n, m, h(n,m))) = (m+1, h(n,m+1)); then H at numerals n and m reduces to the second projection of the m-fold iterate, i.e. the numeral for h(n,m).
proof_roadmap: Define the state-carrying terms H and D (proof lines 1163-1177).
Induction on m: base case through the defining equation of h at 0 (proof lines 1184-1189).
Induction step through the one-step update and final projection (proof lines 1191-1224).
